summary: The basics: charge, voltage and power; AC waves and what meters read; coils, capacitors and magnetism; materials and semiconductors.

blocks.title: Electricity in plain words
items: Current (amperes) is charge on the move: 1 ampere = 1 coulomb per second.
Voltage (volts), also called EMF, is the push between 2 terminals. No complete path, no current.
Resistance (ohms) opposes current. A longer wire has more; halve the area and it doubles.
Power (watts) is how fast energy is used: 1 watt = 1 joule per second.

blocks.title: Fields: capacitors and coils
items: A capacitor is 2 plates and a dielectric. It stores energy in an electrostatic field; capacitance (farads) is charge held per volt.
Current makes a magnetic field; more current, stronger field. Voltage alone makes none.
A changing field induces a voltage in a nearby conductor. Lenz's law: the induced current opposes the change.
A coil stores energy in its magnetic field. More turns, closer turns or a higher-permeability core raise inductance.

blocks.title: Materials
items: Best to worst conductor: silver, copper, aluminum, iron, lead.
At UHF, mica is the best insulator; rubber and wax paper turn lossy.

blocks.title: Semiconductors
items: N-type has extra electrons, P-type a shortage. Their PN junction makes a diode: conducts forward, blocks reverse.
PIV, peak inverse voltage: the most reverse voltage it can block.
Bipolar: small base current controls a large collector current; low input impedance.
FET: almost no gate current, so high input impedance.
Common emitter gives real voltage gain; common collector slightly below 1.

blocks.title: Exam traps
items: TRM isn't a measure. It's RMS, root mean square.
Back EMF is a voltage, not a current.
Joules measure energy, coulombs charge, watts power.
A charged capacitor has voltage but no magnetic field: that takes current.
Lead is a metal: a conductor, not an insulator.
